correctness.summary: After scaling, the weak-Lp ball is characterized by empirical tail inequalities N_y(t)<n t^{-p}. The positive p-Gaussian has exactly the exponential entropy rate of the scaled ell_p ball and satisfies all tail inequalities strictly. A compactly supported perturbation that transfers small mass from below 1 to a higher interval raises differential entropy while preserving the tail inequalities. Compactification preserves both properties. A finite partition with uniform tail slack then produces type classes contained in the weak ball whose Stirling volume exponent is the histogram entropy, which is at least the perturbed density entropy and therefore strictly exceeds the ell_p exponent. This yields a positive lower exponential rate for the volume ratio for every finite p.

limitations: The exponential base C_p is not optimized and the exact asymptotic rate is not determined.
No full large-deviation principle or limiting empirical distribution for the weak Lorentz ball is claimed.
The result concerns finite p and does not address p=infinity.
A non-indexed or differently formulated equivalent result may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Dolezalova--Vybiral (2020) explicitly prove exponential growth only up to p=2 and state the range 2<p<infinity as open, with their particular construction extending only to about p=2.1086. Searches for the exact ratio, weak-Lp/Lorentz volume formulations, the source title and DOI, and later papers citing the source did not locate a solution. Kabluchko--Prochno--Sonnleitner (2023) develops a probabilistic/maximum-entropy approach for Lorentz balls with second index 1, not weak-Lp balls. Prochno--Sonnleitner--Vybiral (2025) cites the 2020 work for coarse volume-radius estimates and studies entropy numbers; its accessible manuscript does not state this volume-ratio result. A non-indexed or differently formulated equivalent result remains possible.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem closes an explicit 2020 open range for the volume comparison of weak and classical finite-dimensional Lebesgue balls. The proof also supplies a reusable mechanism: strict slack in an empirical tail constraint can be converted into a strict high-dimensional volume gain by an entropy-increasing local mass transfer and a type-class construction.
